source: GeoNames CC BY 4.0 modern P-class city IDs/representative WGS84 points; Australian National Archives, NZ Parliament/Ministry for Culture and Heritage, Nouméa municipality, Guam Public Law 24-152, Australian heritage authorities, Federated States of Micronesia/Palau official sources and Tuvalu government plans.
selection: 25 distinct P-class Oceania/Pacific cities, national/territorial capitals or former capitals, excluding Yaren district in Nauru because there is no legal capital and no verified standalone P-class city equivalent. Settlement identity holds are explicit.
coordinateConvention: Modern GeoNames EPSG:4326 latitude/longitude are representative populated-place points; island/atoll, municipality, archaeological site, and government-office-campus extents are distinct geometries.
countryCodeSemantics: Present-day GeoNames sourceCountryCode and PPLC/PPLA/PPLG do not establish past sovereignty or historical capital status and are not authorizations for urban rank.
historicNameScope: Source-grounded legal changes have precise Gregorian dates only where attested; current name projected back to 1801 is provisional and explicitly cannot prove historical name continuity. Government relocations and urban formation do not automatically rename cities.
reviewMethod: GeoNames IDs checked against 214 IDs staged in batches 01–20. Complex situations (Kiribati, Nauru, Palau, Norfolk, Guam) separated from unambiguous urban identities; named city changes and state capital events independently sourced.

heldOutCandidateReviews.reason: Nauru legally has no official capital. Yaren is a district and seat of government, not shown to be an independent P-class city at the capital point. Do not invent a Yaren PPLC or treat its A-class administrative area as a city.

qualityNotes: Previous 20 batches were re-read: 214 unique registered GeoNames IDs and 419 displayTimeline periods; 25 newly selected IDs have zero collisions.
Canberra: Australian National Archives attests 1913-03-12 official naming ceremony; Canberra existed earlier as district name and the ceremony is not proven first habitation.

Wellington and Auckland are separate cities: colonial capital moved permanently Auckland -> Wellington 1865, Parliament first opened in Wellington after move 1865-07-26; Petone initial immigrant settlement differs from modern city centre.
Port Moresby: the harbor was named in 1873 by John Moresby. Harbor naming is not legal modern city creation; Hanuabada and pre-colonial Motu/Koita settlements require separate identity.
Suva became Fiji administrative capital in 1882, formerly Levuka; the transition is a city-to-city political move, not a name change.
Nauru: UNCTAD/OECD record no official capital, government offices in Yaren District. Yaren was deliberately held out, not represented as approved standalone city.
Kiribati GeoNames 2110257 capital Tarawa point is near Bairiki in South Tarawa; distinguish Betio/Bairiki/Ambo urban settlements and Tarawa Atoll polygon.
Tuvalu GeoNames 2110394 Funafuti capital point is in Fongafale. Government offices concentrated in Vaiaku; Funafuti atoll as a whole is not a city polygon.

Palau modern Ngerulmud 8063361 PPLC in Melekeok is a national capitol complex, not verified separately as an urban settlement. Former Koror 1559446 is independent, capital move ~2006; neither record is automatically promoted to a historic 5-level urban rank.
FSM Palikir capital 1989 replaced Kolonia in separate locality; old Kolonia continues as Pohnpei state capital.
Nouméa municipality confirms Port-de-France foundation 1854-06-25 and legally renamed Nouméa on 1866-06-02; French administrative commune status is independent.
Guam original Guam Public Law 24-152 signed 1998-04-08 restores Chamorro municipality official name Hagåtña from Agana; legislative passage 1998-03-25 is not the effective signing date.

Norfolk Kingston first settled 1788, abandoned 1814, resettled 1825 and Pitcairn community in 1856. The inactive interval is a documented historical issue, but no automatic urban eligibility intervals were synthesized.
American Samoa Pago Pago is both harbor and urban region; Fagatogo legislative and Utulei executive functions do not make the separately named villages identical to Pago Pago PPLC.
Saipan GeoNames PPLC has contemporary island/municipality name overlap; independence of an urban town and historical rank unverified.
Unchanged 1801 Korean/English/native name baselines are editorial placeholders, not verified original usage or no-rename attestations.
No GeoNames canonical candidate() filter, five-tier urban ranking, map tiles/manifest, historic border polygon, main branch, app repository, or previous batch files have been altered.
